newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast late crudes creep up with WTI.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast late crudes creep up with WTI.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crude prices crept higher in late discussion, dragged up by a late month rally in West Texas Intermediate (WTI).
WTI batches for November pipeline delivery sold at high prices amid speculative trade, players said.
The rise lifted outright values for Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude five cents to $22.30//22.70 a barrel late Friday.
West Coast buyers said ongoing weakness in refinery margins kept them sidelined. Several considered run cuts to ease the bearish effect of ample stocks, traders said.
Official discounts for ANS remained unchanged at $2.30 a barrel under November WTI.
Ultramar Corp said it would bring several hydroprocessing units late this week for an unspecified period of maintenance.
Wilmington crude held at $18.90/19 a barrel today.
Kern River heavy crude also held, ranging between $17.40 and $17.60, with a major and large independent refiner rumored to offer cargoes. --David Brinkerhoff, Los Angeles energy +1 213 380 2014
